title: Monabaugs (Westhampton)
summary: Monabaugs names a creek, swamp, and pond in the Westhampton area between Potunk and Ketchaponack Necks. The history preserves a water-place name in a landscape where coastal wetlands and waterways have changed over time.
address_label: Westhampton area between Potunk and Ketchaponack Necks, Southampton, NY
history_content: Monabaugs connects creek, swamp, and pond references within one Westhampton water-place context. Dated boundary details appear in the Historic Timeline with their own sources.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Monabaugs and Monobaugs. The name is interpreted as "a deep pond," using a form related to words for deep and pond or water-place. The possessive wording in the records may also preserve a personal name taken from the pond.

Why Place Names Matter

“Names of places are an important aspect of oral history as they become carriers of the past, allowing us a glimpse into occurrences in the past that history books often may have failed to mention.”

— Archive and Public Culture Research Initiative, University of Cape Town, Place Names of Pre-colonial Origin and their Use Today (2012), public project essay, oral-history paragraph
whereintheworld_content: The blue marker is approximate and general. It is placed in the Westhampton landscape between Potunk and Ketchaponack Necks, near but not on top of the existing Apocock and Ketchaponack markers.
